    Efficient ray hooks in essential contours #

    Connect the hook and cohook of a BGRS tackle to the reversed irreducible quiver. Because BGRS composes paths from left to right, its prefix before an efficient hook becomes the suffix after the corresponding reversed-quiver arrow. This file also isolates the separate quiver-prefix improvement interface used by the initial-arrow contour-correction route.

            In an essential ray contour, if one side has at least two arrows then so does the other. Equality with a length-zero path would make the long side invertible, while equality with a length-one path would make it irreducible; both contradict its first-arrow factorization.
